items.summary: The clean committed production runner completed H31-A pilot draw 10 with all eight arm/fold fits. The preregistered paired gate failed and neither same-trace variogram identified a stable range; no later stage ran.
evidence: Run revision 23191e7baa8d22114b713c5c253678e323fff712; 7/7 owner-mirror inputs and 6/6 derived caches verified.
evidence/h31_a/pilot/results.json: mean paired delta -0.0040088545; 1/4 positive folds; metric gate false.
evidence/h31_a/pilot/posthoc_variogram_diagnostics.json: 583 trace groups with pairs; both point fits fail the 95%-sill lag-support diagnostic; no bootstrap interval.
items.impact: The implementation completed end-to-end, but the pilot cannot produce an empirical range or data-derived final buffer. H31-A must stop; no screen or submission is authorized.
items.action: Preserve the pilot artifacts and negative result. Do not tune the same pilot, invent a buffer, or run screen/confirmation; any new attempt requires a preregistered design that can identify the range.

items.summary: H31-A pilot draw 10 failed its paired metric gate, and the residual semivariogram point fits did not reach 95% of the fitted partial sill within observed lag support.
evidence: Mean paired catalogue-gap ΔDTI -0.0040088545; candidate positive in 1/4 blocks versus required >+0.001 mean and at least 3/4 positive blocks.
Furthest populated 500 m lag-bin center 13.75 km; provisional point-fit range about 24.964 km; fitted-sill fraction at support 0.808 for both arms.
No component-bootstrap confidence interval was produced because the point fit was unstable; operational range and final buffer are unknown.
items.impact: The preregistered buffer rule cannot be satisfied. A final spatial holdout buffer cannot be selected, and neither screen nor confirmation is authorized.
items.action: Stop H31-A. Do not use the 24.964 km unstable extrapolation or 500 m pilot collar as the buffer. Preserve this result; only a new preregistration or defensible additional range-identification evidence may justify another attempt.

items.summary: The four-arm detector training run behind evidence/arm_results.json and evidence/operating_point.json was executed in a sibling workspace whose trainer script is not in this repository, so the arm tables cannot be regenerated from a fresh clone.

evidence/oof/*_u16.npz, audited in evidence/oof_quantisation.json, preserve the fold-OOF probability maps, so every downstream step (union, filter, metric, buffer, submission, site) is reproducible from this snapshot.
The site states this limitation next to the reproduction commands rather than implying full end-to-end reproduction.
items.impact: A reviewer cannot re-run the model training; they can re-run everything downstream of it.
items.action: Re-implement the trainer in scripts/run_arms.py with the protocol recorded in registry/experiments.json, and re-check that the union conclusions survive the re-run.

items.summary: The best union gain (+0.0060 off-catalogue proxy DTI) is measured on USGS SGMC state-map faults, a proxy population that resembles but is not the hidden expert-mapped fault set, and no live submission has tested it.
evidence: evidence/union_results.json best_union: LiDAR arm p>=0.60, 106,138 dots, ff_DTI 0.0999 vs incumbent 0.0938.
The incumbent's own dots earn 0.135 credit each on that proxy against 0.025 for the added dots, so the gain is small in per-dot terms even though it is positive.
The catalogue-gap holdout ranks the arms in the opposite order, which is why it is not used as the promotion instrument.
items.impact: The direction is well supported; the magnitude is not, so the file stays research-only and no weekly slot is spent on it.
items.action: Build a second off-catalogue instrument (for example an independent structural-lineament population or the CI-fetched 3DEP scarp population) and require the union to win on both before promotion.

items.summary: The inspected GEMSDOE32 H33 holdout path builds the H33-2 catalogue-flank removal from full labels before evaluating fixed candidate masks against hidden components; it does not appear to recompute the catalogue-derived removal using only fold-visible faults.
evidence: Owner-mirror code at commit 012e17b2a115c3c0d5e7885bea625bf9657c99fc: scripts/run_h33_validation.py reads labels and calls compute_h33_2_flank_sweep(base, labels, d_cat, buffers=(2,3)).
src/gems32/hypotheses33.py compute_h33_2_flank_sweep derives d_cat from labels when not supplied and removes base cells using d_cat.
src/gems32/holdout.py load_holdout_context hides components for the scoring context, but evaluate_candidate_holdout receives a prebuilt static candidate mask.
items.impact: The internal fold result is not an independent hide-and-recover estimate for a catalogue-based deletion method under this project’s preregistered rules. Bias direction is not assumed.
items.action: Do not use the owner-mirror H33 holdout result to promote this method. Any future catalogue-based processing must be rebuilt per fold from visible segments, mask visible faults pixel-exactly, and be tested under the registered evaluator.

items.summary: The inspected GEMSDOE32 H33-2-B2 -zeros GeoTIFF stores finite zeros outside the submission footprint and has no nodata tag, while the official problem-page format states values outside the bounds must be null/NaN.
evidence: Read-only inspection of the public owner-mirror raster at GEMSDOE32 commit 012e17b2a115c3c0d5e7885bea625bf9657c99fc: one float32 band, EPSG:32611, competition-grid transform/shape, no nodata tag, all 7,111,787 cells outside the local pinned footprint finite and equal to zero.
registry/sources.json records the official DrivenData problem-page convention: values outside the competition footprint are null/NaN.
The official sample template is absent in this workspace; the owner-mirror validation receipt is not an organizer validation receipt.
items.impact: This variant does not match the recorded official outside-footprint convention. No claim is made that zero-filled outside values improve the score or were accepted by the organizer.
items.action: Do not use this as a submission format exemplar. For any future candidate use NaN/null outside as specified and validate against an authorized exact sample template; retain all-finite zeros only as a clearly labeled defensive comparison if separately allowed.

items.summary: scripts/prepare_data.py converted only non-finite cells to NaN, so the competition raster's finite -3.4028235e38 nodata sentinel survived into data/prepared/features.f32 for all 19 competition bands (7,110,247 cells outside the footprint plus 3,061 fringe cells inside it), contradicting the documented conversion policy in features.json. The H31-E canary exposed it (derived channels peaked at 3.4e38).
evidence: COMPUTED 2026-10-25: per-band sentinel census of data/training_features.tif (nodata tag -3.4028234663852886e+38); channel-build log showing tophat_det_3 max 3.403e+38 before the fix.

Fix: prepare_data.py now converts the tagged sentinel and |x|>1e30 to NaN; stack rebuilt; det_elev NaN count 7,113,308 exactly equals the sentinel census; src/gemsdoe31/surface_features.py also guards |x|>=1e30 as invalid.
items.impact: Prior arm/OOF artifacts (evidence/arm_results.json, evidence/oof/*) were produced from the pre-fix stack; training and scoring sampled in-footprint cells, so impact is expected negligible but exact equivalence was not re-derived (trainer absent, IR-31-TRAINER-NOT-IN-SNAPSHOT). All H31-E results use the fixed stack.
items.action: Keep the sentinel conversion; any future stack rebuild must re-run the census check.

items.summary: Prior standalone H31-B (gemsdoe31-h31b-scarp-hessian-20261025-37654) placed 97.5% of its 37,654 dots in steep mountain bedrock (piedmont fraction 2.5% vs 30.9% in GEMSDOE32 H33-2-B2 and 52.6% in public catalogue faults), collapsing piedmont off-catalogue DTI (slope <= 6.0 deg) to 0.0052 (vs 0.0586 in GEMSDOE32 B=2) and scoring 0.1171 on gemsdoe31-holdout-v1.
evidence: COMPUTED 2026-10-25 (evidence/h31m_results.json): H31-B piedmont_dot_fraction=0.02494, piedmont_off_sgmc_DTI=0.005167, mountain_off_sgmc_DTI=0.171494.

OWNER-MIRROR GEMSDOE70/GEMSDOE76 README audit: P8-OOF38k beat H33 by +39.8% on mountain-heavy SGMC \ cat (0.1311 vs 0.0938) yet regressed -10.8% live (0.2478 vs 0.2778 USER-REPORTED) because piedmont DTI fell -10.1%.

H31-M restores habitat balance (37.2% piedmont dots, piedmont_off_sgmc_DTI=0.064053 > GEMSDOE32 B=2 0.058617) while beating GEMSDOE32 B=2 on full off-SGMC (0.1010 vs 0.0940) and 4-block off-SGMC (0.1077 vs 0.0984), and scoring 0.1350/0.1372 on gemsdoe31-holdout-v1.
items.impact: Uploading H31-B standalone as primary risked severe live score regression on range-front piedmont and basin-floor faults.
items.action: Promote H31-M (gemsdoe31-h31m-bstep-xmod-submod-20261025-37654) as primary unique submission and reclassify H31-B standalone as archive bedrock specialist (ok_to_download_and_submit=false).

items.summary: 1 m 3DEP LiDAR bands cover 62.1% of the footprint (NE 44.4%, NW 59.2%, SW 85.4%, SE 83.0%) versus 72.1% of public catalogue faults, and NW contains 48.9% of withheld catalogue positives, creating LiDAR-availability propensity confounding and cross-fold base-rate shift in single-head HGB models.
evidence: COMPUTED 2026-10-25: finite step_max coverage by quadrant and catalogue overlap; NW withheld positives 28,641 / 58,625.
items.impact: Single-head trees split on NaN availability as a survey-footprint proxy and produce uncalibrated probabilities across stitched OOF quadrants.
items.action: H31-M trains separate M_sub (full-coverage bands) and M_lidar (strictly within lidar_valid) heads with training-only Bayes prior-odds normalization and quantile marginal alignment.
